clue.text: Time to step out with one like Cinders ?

indicators.note: step out is read as the letters of step put out of order, rearranged

parts.note: an ember is a glowing bit of a dying fire, like a cinder; Cinders is also Cinderella's nickname

explanation.surface: A pantomime-style prompt: it is time for Cinderella, or someone like her, to step out to the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles STEP into SEPT; 'one like Cinders' is not a pantomime heroine but a cinder-like EMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a month of the year, and a month is a period of time.

clue.text: Head of state serving Old English Stew

indicators.note: to stew is to cook ingredients mixed together, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A monarch is served a traditional English stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stew' seems a dish being served; it is a command to jumble SERVING and OE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch, king or queen, is the supreme ruler and head of state.

clue.text: Hazard from a spritely greenhorn

parts.note: read as sprite-like: a peri is a fairy or sprite of Persian myth
L is a learner, a novice, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: Danger comes from a lively novice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spritely' suggests sprightly, lively; here it means a sprite, a PERI, beside L for learner, from the L-plates British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: Danger, a risk of harm.

clue.text: Inscription 'could be happier without the Gorgon's head

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the shuffled letters go around the next piece
could be signals the letters of happier might become something else when rearranged
the head of the Gorgon is the first letter of that word

explanation.surface: Someone could be happier without Medusa's severed head around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges HAPPIER into EPIRAPH, which goes 'without', outside, G, the head of 'Gorgon's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A short quotation or motto inscribed on a building or set at the start of a book.

clue.text: Flowers suitable for an acquiescent Daisy

definitions.meaning: things that bloom
in the song Daisy Bell, Daisy is begged to say yes and ride a bicycle made for two; loose cycling knickers were worn by women riders

explanation.surface: A gardener suggests blooms that would suit a compliant daisy.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomers were baggy knickerbockers worn by Victorian women cyclists, just right for Daisy if she agrees to the bicycle made for two.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowering plants bloom; baggy women's knickers named after Amelia Bloomer were the cycling dress of the 1890s.

clue.text: No tiger music of course.

parts.note: ragtime music is rag
Tiger Rag is a jazz standard; with no tiger, the tiger is out

explanation.surface: Obviously, no tiger could make music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' seems to mean 'naturally'; it is the definition, a dish served as a course. Remove 'Tiger' from the jazz tune Tiger Rag and RAG remains, with the tiger OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A richly seasoned meat stew, served as a course of a meal.

clue.text: Tell in the style of Monte Cristo

definitions.meaning: to tell is an old sense of to number or reckon, as a bank teller does

definitions.text: in the style of Monte Cristo
definitions.meaning: Edmond Dantès styles himself by a noble title in Dumas's novel

explanation.surface: A request to recount a story the way Dumas's hero would.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell money is to reckon it; the hero of Dumas's novel goes by a nobleman's title, the Count of Monte Cristo.

clue.text: Cue for this producer of 10

definitions.meaning: in billiards, a shot striking two balls in turn, played with a cue
10 across is the firing of guns, which a big gun produces

explanation.surface: A prompt for something that makes the noise at 10.
explanation.definitionFit: A billiards stroke hitting both object balls; also a large gun that fires shells.

clue.text: Runs a live sort of joint

indicators.note: sort here works as a verb, to arrange, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone runs a lively kind of nightspot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' looks like a bar or club; it is the mechanical coupling. 'sort of' rearranges RUNS A LIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupling that lets a shaft turn at an angle in any direction, short for the full name of that joint.

clue.text: Jolly lot, somewhat hot ?

definitions.meaning: a Jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, so the Jolly lot is ..., the corps as a whole
a unit of heat, a measure of some warmth

explanation.surface: A cheerful group gets a bit warm.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Marines are THE RM; a Jolly is old naval slang for a marine.
explanation.definitionFit: A British unit of heat, 100,000 British thermal units, once used for gas bills; the marines as a body are the RM.

clue.text: Feeling all in a whirl I go by Forest Green

indicators.note: by places one piece beside the other, here the green word before the travelling words

parts.note: vert is the heraldic word for green, and in old forest law the green growth of a forest

explanation.surface: Someone dizzily driving past Forest Green, a small Gloucestershire place with a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Forest Green looks like a place name; it is VERT, green in heraldry and forest law. Forest Green Rovers is an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Dizziness is the sensation that one's surroundings are spinning.

clue.text: Army discharge

parts.note: reads like a soldier leaving the service, but means the firing of weapons by an army

explanation.definitionFit: The shooting of guns is what an army discharges in battle.

clue.text: Authority required for a straight line

definitions.meaning: a person holding power, such as a king or governor
the drawing instrument with a straight edge

explanation.surface: Officialdom insisting everyone toe a straight line.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is an authority who governs; the measuring stick with a straight edge guides a pencil along a line.

clue.text: Magnificent edifice for somebody ?

parts.note: somebody is read as some body, a corpse, so the grand building is a tomb

explanation.definitionFit: A grand tomb, named after King Mausolus, is a stately building housing a dead body.

clue.text: Unskilled, needing me for a tricky experiment

indicators.note: a tricky experiment is one whose letters are tangled, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters that are left over beside the answer

explanation.surface: A clumsy scientist confesses that a difficult experiment needs their help to go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: 'tricky' rearranges EXPERIMENT, which holds the answer plus ME; so the answer is what remains of the shuffled letters once ME is set aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking expertise means having no skill.

clue.text: Still one has a moving ex experience on this flight

definitions.text: Still one has a moving ex experience on this flight

parts.words: Still one has a moving ex experience on this flight
parts.note: a flight here is a flight of stairs: standing still, one is carried up it

explanation.definitionFit: A moving staircase, a flight of steps that carries people who stand still.

clue.text: One thing flowing backwards in Hohenlinden?

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: flowing backwards tells us the word for thing runs in reverse

parts.note: res is the Latin for a thing

explanation.surface: Something seems to run upstream in a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Campbell's poem Hohenlinden, on a Napoleonic battle in Bavaria, describes 'the flow of Iser, rolling rapidly'; 'flowing' doubles as a river hint in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The river is the Bavarian waterway named in Campbell's poem about that battle.

clue.text: Rude noise coming from the cane

definitions.meaning: a blowing noise made with the tongue to jeer
a soft red fruit grown on canes

explanation.surface: A schoolchild makes a rude noise after being caned.
explanation.definitionFit: A derisive blowing sound, from rhyming slang for a breeze; also a red berry fruit grown on canes.

clue.text: Carmen's author's flourishes

definitions.meaning: Prosper Mérimée wrote the novella Carmen, so this is his first name with a possessive
thrives, does well

explanation.surface: The writer of Carmen has some decorative flourishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmen, the source of Bizet's opera, was written by Prosper Mérimée; to thrive is to do well.

clue.text: Fix price, of the odd pair in the recess

indicators.note: in puts the shuffled pair inside the church recess

parts.note: an apse is a recess at the end of a church

indicators.note: an odd pair is a strange one, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two odd items in an alcove get priced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recess' sounds like a break; in a church it is an apse. 'odd' scrambles the pair before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To value something is to set or estimate its price.

clue.text: Anatomical impudence

definitions.meaning: read as a part of the body, the one between head and shoulders
cheek, brass nerve

explanation.surface: A rude anatomy lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: The body part joining head to torso; also slang for cheeky boldness, as in 'what a nerve'.

clue.text: Contends with record return in fruit

indicators.note: in places the turned record within the fruit

parts.note: grapes are a fruit

indicators.note: return means the word for record comes back the other way

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: Someone struggles with a record of profit returned in the fruit trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' is the long-playing disc, and 'return' turns it before it goes into the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrestle with a problem is to struggle against it.

clue.text: Christmas is coming This, too, even earlier

definitions.text: Christmas is coming This, too, even earlier

parts.words: Christmas is coming This, too, even earlier
parts.note: the season of approach before the holiday arrives sooner still

explanation.definitionFit: The church season of the four weeks before Christmas, marking its approach.

clue.text: How piano-players play ?

parts.note: piano is the musical direction meaning quietly, so players following it play gently

explanation.definitionFit: Quietly, gently: the meaning of the Italian marking piano.

clue.text: So tuneful the plot of Keats's nightingale

definitions.meaning: full of melody, sweet-sounding
in Ode to a Nightingale the bird sings 'in some ... plot of beechen green'

explanation.surface: A remark that the storyline of Keats's ode is very musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' looks like a storyline; in Keats's ode it is a patch of ground, and the word describing it is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet-sounding and pleasant to hear; Keats calls the nightingale's patch of beech wood by this word in his ode.

clue.text: Little woman's progress

definitions.meaning: Louisa May Alcott's Little Women are the four sisters Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy of that surname
advance, walk steadily onward

explanation.surface: A small woman's advance.
explanation.definitionFit: The sisters of Little Women share this surname; to stride forward in step is to progress.

clue.text: Shape of a girl's best friend

definitions.text: Shape of a girl's best friend

parts.words: Shape of a girl's best friend
parts.note: diamonds are a girl's best friend, and the diamond outline is a geometric figure

explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus, the diamond figure with four equal sides, is the shape of a diamond.

clue.text: Dismissed due to being tiddly

indicators.note: tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sacked for being drunk at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tiddly', British slang for tipsy, rearranges DUE TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposed or put out, as a batsman is out; sent away.

clue.text: Go back to Innisfree for instance

definitions.meaning: withdraw, fall back
Yeats's Lake Isle of Innisfree is a peaceful hideaway

explanation.surface: A suggestion to return to the Irish isle of Yeats's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw is to go back; Yeats's island in the poem is a quiet refuge from the world.

clue.text: He chucks out a quarter to the winner

parts.note: E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass
a victor is the one who wins

explanation.surface: A bouncer is described as throwing out someone, a quarter of an hour before the victor arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarter to' sounds like telling the time; a quarter is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord who expels a tenant is the person doing the chucking out.

clue.text: Wood in King Arthur's time

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A forest from the days of Camelot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Arthur's time' looks like the definition of an era; the answer lies within 'Arthur's time'. The word survives in English place names such as Lyndhurst.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a wooded hill or copse.

clue.text: The old street ready for repair not long since

parts.note: ye is an old spelling of the

indicators.note: something for repair is broken, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old street that is ready to be mended.
explanation.walkthrough: YE is a mock-antique spelling of 'the', from the old letter thorn printed as Y; 'for repair' scrambles ST plus READY.
explanation.definitionFit: The day before today, a short time ago.
